sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2005. Is there a boundary between Plateau and Jukunoid? Draft paper for the Vienna Jukunoid workshop, 19-20 Nov 2005
sources.note: Zero mentions of Kapya (grep count 0). Sec. 2.3 Tones is about Plateau vs Jukunoid tone systems ('four and five-tone systems characteristic of some Jukunoid languages'); no stress. Sec. 1.3.2 lists the Jukunoid data sources (Shimizu 1980a,b; Dykstra n.d.; Priest & Priest n.d.; Koops 1990, n.d.; Storch; Vienna project).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record kapy1238 (Hammarström et al.), incl. 'meds' list and reference records 714024, 302077, 309353
sources.note: No descriptive work with a phonology of Kapya. Most-extensive descriptions: Prischnegg 2008 (coded phonology_or_text, 30 pp bearing on Kapya) and R. Koops 1994 'The sounds of Kapya --- tentative analysis', 6 pp, unpublished ms (ref 714024, coded wordlist_or_less). Neither online.

sources.citation: Kempf, Viktoria & Tamara Prischnegg. 2020. A sketch of Akum (Southern Jukunoid). Afrika und Übersee 93: 298-326. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.215
sources.note: Nothing about Kapya beyond naming it as a Southern Jukunoid member (p. 305: 'the whole Southern Jukunoid language group (Bezen, Bete, Lufu, Akum, Kuteb, Yukuben, Kapya)'). Its phonology section (2.3 Tone, p. 306) describes AKUM: 'Akum has a three-tone system... we only find lexically distinctive tones'; no stress statement for any language.

sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project / ELCat entry 4406 'Kapya' (main page and bibliography), Wayback copies 2015/2019
sources.note: Nothing; bibliography consists only of Ethnologue 16 (2009) and the World Oral Literature Project; 'No documents have been added'. Classification Jukunoid, Yukuben-Kuteb; 200 speakers (2004).

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2013. Ethnologue 17, entry 'Kapya' (Wayback copy 2014); also Ethnologue 24 (2021) paywalled shell
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. 'Population 200 (2004). Location Taraba State, Takum LGA, at Kapya. Language Status 6b (Threatened). Dialects Related to Kutep [kub].'

sources.citation: English Wikipedia: 'Kapya language', 'Jukunoid languages', 'Yukubenic languages' (raw wikitext)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Cites Blench 2026 'Rethinking the classification of South Jukunoid' (Bantoid 3, Buffalo, May 2026; academia.edu/167541631) for Kuteb–Kapya as an independent Benue-Congo branch; Blench 2019 Atlas of Nigerian Languages (4th ed.) for location; Kapya numerals (tone-marked) from Chan's Numeral Systems site.
